subject: Scaling workshop & sizing: ACME Payments — next steps
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmepayments.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops+infra@acmepayments.com, ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Intro call — throughput & latency overview

Hi Karthik and Ava,

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — appreciate the walkthrough. As discussed, our engineering team would like to do a focused sizing workshop to validate throughput/latency targets and expected token distribution before we commit to a Dedicated pool.

Quick recap of what we covered on the call:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~250 requests/sec (burst to 400 for short periods)
- Average request size: ~450 tokens (user + system + expected response)
- Latency target (p50/p95): 120ms / 350ms for 512-token responses
- Primary model family: gpt-large-like open weights (we're evaluating cost vs perf)
- Security: SOC2 and VPC peering required — we'll share the questionnaire once we move past sizing

Can we lock in a 60–90 minute workshop next week to run throughput simulations and walk through your sizing template? Attendees from our side would be myself, a senior infra engineer (ops+infra@acmepayments.com), and our ML infra lead (I can confirm name once I check with them).

Proposed windows (ET):
- Tue 7/20: 10:00–11:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Wed 7/21: 09:00–10:30

If you have a standard agenda or a pre-populated sizing sheet, please share so we can come prepared. Attaching my notes from the discovery call.

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Platform
ACME Payments

Attachment: discovery-notes.pdf (text summary)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmepayments.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Scaling workshop & sizing: ACME Payments — next steps

Liam — thanks for the clear recap and the windows. 15:00–16:30 ET on Tue 7/20 works well for our team; I'll hold that and send a calendar invite unless you prefer a different slot.

Agenda we'll cover in the workshop (high level):
1) Review your traffic profile and token mix (confirm p50/p95 sizes)
2) Walk through our sizing template and baseline throughput curves
3) Run a few hypothetical configs (batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs) and show cost/latency estimates
4) Next steps: Dedicated pool sizing recommendation + timeline to prototype

Before the session can you confirm:
- Expected sustained qps vs burst (you mentioned 250 sustained, 400 burst — is burst duration ~5–15 minutes?)
- % of requests requiring long-context (>= 2k tokens) vs short (<= 512 tokens)
- Any hard p99 constraint (we assume p95 is primary for UX)

I've attached our quick-sizing template — filling the fields below will let us pre-run estimates and make the call productive: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx

I'll also invite our ML infra lead (Ava) and Solutions Architect (Stephanie) so we can answer kernel/quantization questions live. If you want us to include a short demo of our runtime in the call, we can carve out 10–15 minutes.

Talk soon,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx
From: ava_chen@redwood.com <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-16T14:20:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Scaling workshop & sizing: ACME Payments — prep notes

Karthik / Stephanie — forwarding Liam's note and the discovery PDF. Quick checklist for the workshop prep:
- I'll pre-fill token distribution (short/long) examples based on their notes and common payments flows
- Steph, please bring the quantization matrix and a couple of kernels we recommend for gpt-large-like families
- Karthik, do you want me to run a micro-benchmark (1k simulated qps at 512 tokens) and include latency curves? I can upload results ahead of the meeting.

Also, we should have the canary configs ready (1) 2x small GPUs optimized for latency, (2) 4x quantized GPUs for throughput/cost. Will collect cost delta estimates.

—Ava
Senior ML Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks, team. 15:00–16:30 ET on Tue 7/20 is confirmed from our side. I've added the calendar invite (link below) and included our infra lead, Priya Shah (priya.shah@acmepayments.com), on the event.

Quick answers before the call:
- Sustained qps: 230–260 for most of the day; bursts to ~420 for 8–12 minutes during peak reconciliation windows
- Long-context usage: ~8% of requests will be >= 2k tokens; majority are <= 600 tokens
- p99: Our internal SLAs are more conservative, but for user-facing flows we care about p95 primarily — p99 is a secondary metric we track for incident triage
